questions.solution: __Shortcut Trick__ Identify diameters: d₁ = AB = 2, d₂ = AC = 2 + BC, and d₃ = AD = 3 + BC. Condition: Middle Area = Average of others ⇒ d₂² = (d₁² + d₃²) / 2. 2(2 + BC)² = 2² + (3 + BC)² ⇒ 2(4 + 4BC + BC²) = 4 + 9 + 6BC + BC². 8 + 8BC + 2BC² = 13 + 6BC + BC² ⇒ BC² + 2BC − 5 = 0. Solving for BC using the quadratic formula: BC = −1 + √6. **∴ The correct answer is (√6) − 1 cm.**

questions.question:
A = Area of the largest circle drawn inside a square of side 1 cm.

B = Sum of areas of 4 identical (largest possible) circles drawn inside a square of side 1 cm.

C = Sum of areas of 9 identical circle (largest possible) drawn inside a square of side 1 cm.

D = Sum of area of 16 identical circles (largest possible) drawn inside a square of side 1 cm.

Which of the following is TRUE about A, B, C and D?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If a square of side 's' is filled with n² identical circles in an n × n grid, the radius of each circle is r = s / (2n).

The sum of the areas of these n² circles = n² × π × r² = n² × π × (s / 2n)².

Total Area = n² × π × s² / (4n²) = πs² / 4.

Since the total area depends only on the side of the square (s), and here s = 1 cm for all cases, the area remains constant.

**∴ The correct answer is A = B = C = D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Side of square = 1 cm.

Formula: Area of circle = πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b50e5c8cb661dc65f25a399cf2e473a32515f3d25e0f14004058d6b659be699.png] 

⇒ Case A: Largest circle inside square of side 1 cm → Diameter = 1 cm, Radius (r) = 1/2 cm.

⇒ Area A = π × (1/2)² = π/4 cm².

⇒ Case B: 4 identical circles (2 × 2 grid) → Diameter of each = 1/2 cm, Radius (r) = 1/4 cm.

⇒ Area B = 4 × [π × (1/4)²] = 4 × π/16 = π/4 cm².

⇒ Case C: 9 identical circles (3 × 3 grid) → Diameter of each = 1/3 cm, Radius (r) = 1/6 cm.

⇒ Area C = 9 × [π × (1/6)²] = 9 × π/36 = π/4 cm².

⇒ Case D: 16 identical circles (4 × 4 grid) → Diameter of each = 1/4 cm, Radius (r) = 1/8 cm.

⇒ Area D = 16 × [π × (1/8)²] = 16 × π/64 = π/4 cm².

⇒ Comparing all values: A = B = C = D = π/4 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is A = B = C = D.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circle Inscribed in a Square

When a circle is inscribed in a square of side 's', the diameter of the circle is always equal to the side of the square. Area = (π/4) × s².

Packing Efficiency

The ratio of the area of the circles to the area of the square is π/4 ≈ 0.785. This means the circles always occupy approximately 78.5% of the square's area, regardless of the number of grid circles.

Square Inscribed in a Circle

When a square is inscribed in a circle of radius 'r', the diagonal of the square equals the diameter of the circle (2r). Area of square = 2r².</p

questions.question: A prism has a square base whose side is 8 cm. The height of the prism is 80 cm. The prism is cut into 10 identical parts by 9 cuts which are parallel to the base of the prism. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of all the 10 parts together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Each horizontal cut creates 2 new base surfaces.

Total surface area = (Initial surface area) + (2 × Number of cuts × Base Area)

Initial TSA = (2 × 8 × 8) + (4 × 8 × 80) = 128 + 2560 = 2688 cm²

Added area from 9 cuts = 2 × 9 × (8 × 8) = 18 × 64 = 1152 cm²

Total TSA = 2688 + 1152 = 3840 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3840 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Square base side (a) = 8 cm, Height (h) = 80 cm, Number of parts = 10 (using 9 cuts).

Formula used: TSA of prism = (2 × Base Area) + (Base Perimeter × Height)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/558208110860dce9c379be06383975af86163e3106340d9511f3266f382e9379.png] 

⇒ Base Area of the prism = side² = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

⇒ Perimeter of the base = 4 × side = 4 × 8 = 32 cm

⇒ Height of each identical part = Total height ÷ 10 = 80 ÷ 10 = 8 cm

⇒ TSA of one part = (2 × Base Area) + (Perimeter × Height of one part)

⇒ TSA of one part = (2 × 64) + (32 × 8) = 128 + 256 = 384 cm²

⇒ Total TSA of all 10 parts = 10 × 384 = 3840 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3840 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prism Properties

A prism is a 3D solid with two identical parallel bases. Volume = Base Area × Height. Lateral Surface Area (LSA) = Perimeter of base × Height.

Effect of Cutting

When a solid is cut parallel to its base, the number of additional surfaces created is 2 × (Number of cuts). Each new surface area equals the base area.

Total Surface Area Formula

For any prism, TSA = LSA + 2 × Base Area. If it is cut into 'n' parts, the combined TSA = Original LSA + (2 × n × Base Area).</p

questions.question: A cone of radius 90 cm and height 120 cm stands on its base. It is cut into 3 parts by 2 cuts parallel to its base such that the height of the three parts (from top to bottom) are in ratio of 1 ∶ 2 ∶ 3. What is the total surface area (in cm²) of the middle part?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of heights of parts = 1 : 2 : 3 ⇒ Cumulative height ratios = 1 : (1+2) : (1+2+3) = 1 : 3 : 6.

Since the cone is similar, radii ratio = height ratio = 1 : 3 : 6.

Given total radius = 90 cm (6 units), so radii of cuts are 15 cm (1 unit) and 45 cm (3 units).

Middle part height = 120 × (2/6) = 40 cm; Slant height l = √(40² + (45−15)²) = 50 cm.

TSA of middle part (frustum) = π(r₁ + r₂)l + πr₁² + πr₂² = π(60 × 50 + 225 + 2025) = 5250π.

TSA = 5250 × 22/7 = 16500 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 16500 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of large cone (R) = 90 cm, Height (H) = 120 cm.

Ratio of heights of three parts (top to bottom) = 1 : 2 : 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ec098798f1af19802de5e41483155839dc17496d6fd7abaade8afe9238c9a15.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Radius at any height h' from vertex: r = (h'/H) × R

Slant height of frustum: l = √(h² + (r₂ − r₁)²)

Total Surface Area of frustum = π(r₁ + r₂)l + πr₁² + πr₂²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total segments of height = 1 + 2 + 3 = 6 units.

⇒ 6 units = 120 cm ⇒ 1 unit = 20 cm.

⇒ Height of top part = 20 cm; Height of middle part = 40 cm; Height of bottom part = 60 cm.

⇒ Height from vertex to top of middle part (h₁) = 20 cm.

⇒ Height from vertex to bottom of middle part (h₂) = 20 + 40 = 60 cm.

⇒ Radius at h₁ (r₁) = (20/120) × 90 = 15 cm.

⇒ Radius at h₂ (r₂) = (60/120) × 90 = 45 cm.

⇒ Slant height of middle part (l) = √(40² + (45 − 15)²) = √(1600 + 900) = 50 cm.

⇒ TSA = π × (15 + 45) × 50 + π × (15)² + π × (45)²

⇒ TSA = π × (3000 + 225 + 2025) = 5250 × (22/7)

⇒ TSA = 750 × 22 = 16500 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 16500 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Frustum of a Cone

The volume is given by V = (1/3)πh(r₁² + r₂² + r₁r₂), where h is the vertical height of the frustum.

Ratio of Volumes in Cut Cones

If a cone is cut by planes parallel to the base, the ratio of the volumes of the resulting smaller cones is equal to the ratio of the cubes of their corresponding heights: V₁/V₂ = (h₁/h₂)³.

Slant Height of a Cone

The slant height (L) of a full cone with radius R and height H is calculated using the Pythagorean theorem: L = √(R² + H²).</p

questions.question: The curved surface area of a cylinder is 594 cm² and its volume is 1336.5 cm³. What is the height (in cm) of the cylinder?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Volume (V) to Curved Surface Area (CSA) for a cylinder is always r/2.

r/2 = V ÷ CSA = 1336.5 ÷ 594 = 2.25

Radius (r) = 2.25 × 2 = 4.5 cm

Now, CSA = 2πrh ⇒ 594 = 2 × (22/7) × 4.5 × h

h = (594 × 7) ÷ (2 × 22 × 4.5) = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 594 cm²

Volume (V) = 1336.5 cm³

Formula Used: CSA = 2πrh and Volume = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a5ab4a83466efd33138298dcc85081611732a0beb6838675bbc23ac73b80c3c3.png] 

Dividing Volume by CSA:

⇒ (πr²h) ÷ (2πrh) = 1336.5 ÷ 594

⇒ r / 2 = 2.25

⇒ r = 2.25 × 2 = 4.5 cm

Substitute the value of r in the CSA formula:

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 4.5 × h = 594

⇒ (44/7) × (9/2) × h = 594

⇒ (198/7) × h = 594

⇒ h = (594 × 7) ÷ 198

⇒ h = 3 × 7

⇒ h = 21 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 21 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of a Cylinder

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(r + h).

Relationship between V, CSA, and Radius

For any cylinder, the radius r can be directly found if Volume (V) and CSA are known: r = 2V ÷ CSA.

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

If R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius, Volume = π(R² − r²)h.</p

questions.question: A hollow cylinder is made up of metal. The difference between the outer and the inner curved surface area of this cylinder is 352 cm². The height of the cylinder is 28 cm. If the total surface area of this hollow cylinder is 2640 cm², then what are the inner and outer radii (in cm)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in CSA = 2 × (22/7) × h × (R − r) ⇒ 352 = 2 × (22/7) × 28 × (R − r) ⇒ R − r = 2 cm.

TSA = 2 × (22/7) × (R + r) × (h + R − r) ⇒ 2640 = 2 × (22/7) × (R + r) × (28 + 2).

2640 = (1320/7) × (R + r) ⇒ (R + r) = (2640 × 7) / 1320 = 14 cm.

Solving R − r = 2 and R + r = 14 gives Outer radius R = 8 cm and Inner radius r = 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm and 8 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Difference in Curved Surface Area = 352 cm², Height (h) = 28 cm, Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2640 cm².

**Formula Used:** Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh; Total Surface Area of hollow cylinder = 2πRh + 2πrh + 2π(R² − r²).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f29e17c90c731b781285a4e3fdec5c0e0f89b17fb58b038bebd2959c11893da.png] 

⇒ Difference in CSA = 2πRh − 2πrh = 2πh(R − r) = 352

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × 28 × (R − r) = 352

⇒ 176 × (R − r) = 352 ⇒ R − r = 2 cm --- (i)

⇒ TSA = 2πh(R + r) + 2π(R² − r²) = 2640

⇒ 2π(R + r)[h + (R − r)] = 2640

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × (R + r) × [28 + 2] = 2640

⇒ (44/7) × (R + r) × 30 = 2640

⇒ (R + r) = (2640 × 7) / 1320 = 14 cm --- (ii)

⇒ Adding (i) and (ii): 2R = 16 ⇒ R = 8 cm

⇒ Subtracting (i) from (ii): 2r = 12 ⇒ r = 6 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm and 8 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Hollow Cylinder

The volume of the material in a hollow cylinder is given by V = πh(R² − r²), where R is the outer radius and r is the inner radius.

Thickness of the Wall

The thickness of the wall of a hollow cylinder is the difference between the outer and inner radii, calculated as T = R − r.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

For a solid cylinder, CSA = 2πrh. For a hollow cylinder, the total curved surface area includes both the inner and outer surfaces: 2πh(R + r).</p

questions.question: A solid metal sphere has radius 14 cm. It is melted to form small cones of radius 1.75 cm and height 3.5 cm. How many small cones will be obtained from the sphere?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Number of cones (n) = Volume of Sphere ÷ Volume of 1 Cone

n = (4/3 × π × R³) ÷ (1/3 × π × r² × h) = (4 × R³) ÷ (r² × h)

n = (4 × 14 × 14 × 14) ÷ (1.75 × 1.75 × 3.5)

n = 10976 ÷ 10.71875 = 1024

**∴ The correct answer is 1024 cones.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the sphere (R) = 14 cm

Radius of each cone (r) = 1.75 cm = 7/4 cm

Height of each cone (h) = 3.5 cm = 7/2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a sphere = (4/3) × π × R³

Volume of a cone = (1/3) × π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4267b95a185199c85542f5c212e2f402468e3b7a016fd6900d388f03285b001.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of Sphere = (4/3) × π × (14)³

⇒ Volume of n Cones = n × (1/3) × π × (7/4)² × (7/2)

⇒ (4/3) × π × 14 × 14 × 14 = n × (1/3) × π × (7/4) × (7/4) × (7/2)

⇒ 4 × 14 × 14 × 14 = n × (7 × 7 × 7) / (4 × 4 × 2)

⇒ 4 × (14/7) × (14/7) × (14/7) = n / (32)

⇒ 4 × 2 × 2 × 2 = n / 32

⇒ 32 = n / 32

⇒ n = 32 × 32

⇒ n = 1024

**∴ The correct answer is 1024 cones.**

**__Additional Information__**

Melting and Recasting Rule

When a solid object is melted to form new objects of different shapes, the total volume of the material remains constant throughout the process.

Volume of Sphere

The volume of a sphere with radius R is given by the formula V = (4/3)πR³.

Volume of Cone

The volume of a cone with radius r and height h is given by the formula V = (1/3)πr²h.

Surface Area of Sphere

The total surface area (TSA) of a sphere is 4πR², which is four times the area of its great circle.</p

questions.question: A metallic hemispherical bowl is made up of steel. The total steel used in making the bowl is 342π cm³. The bowl can hold 144π cm³ water. What is the thickness (in cm) of bowl and the curved surface area (in cm²) of outer side?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Internal Volume (capacity) → (2/3)πr³ = 144π ⇒ r³ = 216 ⇒ Inner radius (r) = 6 cm.

Material Volume = (2/3)π(R³ − r³) = 342π ⇒ R³ − 216 = 513 ⇒ R³ = 729 ⇒ Outer radius (R) = 9 cm.

Thickness = Outer radius − Inner radius = 9 − 6 = 3 cm.

Outer Curved Surface Area = 2πR² = 2π × 9² = 162π cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 3 cm, 162π cm².**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Volume of steel used (Material) = 342π cm³

Internal capacity (Volume of water) = 144π cm³

**Formula Used:**

1. Volume of Hemisphere = (2/3)πr³

2. Volume of Hollow Hemisphere = (2/3)π(R³ − r³)

3. Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Hemisphere = 2πr²

4. Thickness = R − r (where R = Outer radius, r = Inner radius)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/388a0af0a9237d6a3c18cf77141779ab4fd18a36a7af3284a3ca8bceb476f017.png] 

Let the outer radius be R and the inner radius be r.

Step 1: Find the inner radius (r) using capacity.

⇒ (2/3) × π × r³ = 144π

⇒ r³ = 144 × (3/2)

⇒ r³ = 72 × 3 = 216

⇒ r = 6 cm

Step 2: Find the outer radius (R) using the volume of steel.

⇒ (2/3) × π × (R³ − r³) = 342π

⇒ R³ − 6³ = 342 × (3/2)

⇒ R³ − 216 = 171 × 3

⇒ R³ − 216 = 513

⇒ R³ = 513 + 216 = 729

⇒ R = 9 cm

Step 3: Calculate Thickness and Outer CSA.

⇒ Thickness = R − r = 9 − 6 = 3 cm

⇒ Outer CSA = 2 × π × R²

⇒ Outer CSA = 2 × π × 9²

⇒ Outer CSA = 2 × π × 81 = 162π cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 3 cm, 162π cm².**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Hollow Hemisphere

TSA = Outer CSA + Inner CSA + Area of base ring = 2πR² + 2πr² + π(R² − r²) = 3πR² + πr².

Volume and CSA of Solid Hemisphere

For a solid hemisphere of radius r: Volume = (2/3)πr³, CSA = 2πr², and TSA = 3πr².

Sphere Formulas

For a sphere of radius R: Volume = (4/3)πR³ and Surface Area = 4πR².</p

questions.question: There is a box of cuboid shape. The smallest side of the box is 20 cm and largest side is 40 cm. Which of the following can be volume (in cm³) of the box?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume Range = (Smallest × Smallest × Largest) to (Smallest × Largest × Largest)

Minimum Volume = 20 × 20 × 40 = 16,000 cm³

Maximum Volume = 20 × 40 × 40 = 32,000 cm³

Range: 16,000 ≤ Volume ≤ 32,000

Only 18,000 cm³ lies within this range.

**∴ The correct answer is 18000 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Smallest side (a) = 20 cm

Largest side (c) = 40 cm

Let the third side be 'b' cm.

**Formula:**

Volume of Cuboid = Length × Width × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f4c58ea24528305c1a76ad48685befd1f009451c0579bebcd2f1beb8a83e96d9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ According to the condition, 20 ≤ b ≤ 40

⇒ Volume (V) = 20 × b × 40

⇒ V = 800b

⇒ Substituting the minimum value of b = 20: Vₘᵢₙ = 800 × 20 = 16,000 cm³

⇒ Substituting the maximum value of b = 40: Vₘₐₓ = 800 × 40 = 32,000 cm³

⇒ The possible volume must satisfy: 16,000 ≤ V ≤ 32,000

⇒ Among the options (18000, 12000, 36000, 42000), only 18,000 falls in this range.

**∴ The correct answer is 18000 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cuboid

The total area of all six faces is given by TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), where l, b, and h are the dimensions.

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal, D = √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four vertical walls (excluding top and bottom) is LSA = 2h(l + b).</p

questions.question: A pyramid has a square base, whose side is 8 cm. If the height of pyramid is 16 cm, then what is the total surface area (in cm²) of the pyramid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Surface Area (TSA) = Base Area + 4 × (Area of one triangular face)

Base Area = 8 × 8 = 64 cm²

Slant height (l) = √[Height² + (side/2)²] = √[16² + 4²] = √272 = 4√17 cm

LSA = 2 × side × slant height = 2 × 8 × 4√17 = 64√17 cm²

TSA = 64 + 64√17 = 64(√17 + 1) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 64(√17 + 1) cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Side of square base (a) = 8 cm, Height of pyramid (h) = 16 cm.

**Formula:** TSA = a² + 2al, where l = slant height.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bdafbdee2008b973cb5fb2795c773dbe150fb694ac80f0fb7a18256fb85cdc88.png] 

⇒ Slant height (l) = √[h² + (a/2)²]

⇒ l = √[16² + (8/2)²]

⇒ l = √[256 + 16] = √272

⇒ l = √[16 × 17] = 4√17 cm

⇒ Total Surface Area (TSA) = Area of Base + Area of 4 Triangular faces

⇒ TSA = a² + 4 × (1/2 × a × l)

⇒ TSA = a² + 2al

⇒ TSA = 8² + 2 × 8 × 4√17

⇒ TSA = 64 + 64√17

⇒ TSA = 64(√17 + 1) cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 64(√17 + 1) cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Pyramid

The volume (V) of any pyramid is given by V = (1/3) × Base Area × Vertical Height (h).

Slant Height vs Slant Edge

Slant height (l) is the altitude of a triangular face, while Slant Edge (e) is the length from the apex to a base corner: e = √[h² + (d/2)²], where d is the base diagonal.

General Lateral Surface Area

For a regular pyramid, LSA = (1/2) × Perimeter of base × Slant height.</p

questions.question: What is the value of frac{{2( {1{{ }} - {{ }}{{sin }²}{{theta }}} ){{cose}}{{{c}}²}{{theta }}}}{{{{cot }²}{{theta }}( {1{{ }} + {{ }}{{tan }²}{{theta }}} )}} - 1?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 45° to simplify the expression quickly.

Numerator = 2(1 − sin²45°) × csc²45° = 2(1 − 1/2) × 2 = 2 × 1/2 × 2 = 2.

Denominator = cot²45° (1 + tan²45°) = 1 × (1 + 1) = 2.

Value = (Numerator ÷ Denominator) − 1 = (2 ÷ 2) − 1 = 0.

Check options: cos (2 × 45°) = cos 90° = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is cos 2θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [2(1 − sin²θ) csc²θ] ÷ [cot²θ (1 + tan²θ)] − 1

**Formula Used:** 1 − sin²θ = cos²θ; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; cos 2θ = 2 cos²θ − 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4762cda55024fce401ba2f6d71f17fb95a1e6bcd51e77c7aae5c5c77d0eed089.png] 

⇒ Expression = [2 (cos²θ) csc²θ] ÷ [cot²θ (sec²θ)] − 1

⇒ Expression = [2 (cos²θ / sin²θ)] ÷ [cot²θ sec²θ] − 1

⇒ Expression = [2 cot²θ] ÷ [cot²θ sec²θ] − 1

⇒ Expression = 2 ÷ sec²θ − 1

⇒ Expression = 2 cos²θ − 1

⇒ Using identity cos 2θ = 2 cos²θ − 1

**∴ The correct answer is cos 2θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Standard relations include sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ, and 1 + cot²θ = csc²θ.

Double Angle Formulas for Cosine

cos 2θ can be expressed as cos²θ − sin²θ, or 2 cos²θ − 1, or 1 − 2 sin²θ.

Reciprocal Relations

csc θ = 1/sin θ, sec θ = 1/cos θ, and cot θ = cos θ/sin θ.</p

questions.question: What is the value of frac{{cos 2{{A }} + {{ }}2{{cos }²}{{A }} - {{ }}2cos 2{{A}}cos {{A}}}}{{sin 2{{A }} - {{ }}2{{sin }²}{{A}}sin 2{{A}}}} if A = 30°?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Directly substitute A = 30° into the expression.

Numerator = cos 60° + 2cos² 30° − 2cos 60° cos 30° = 1/2 + 2(3/4) − 2(1/2)(√3/2) = 1/2 + 3/2 − √3/2 = (4 − √3)/2.

Denominator = sin 60° − 2sin² 30° sin 60° = sin 60° (1 − 2sin² 30°) = sin 60° cos 60° = (√3/2) × (1/2) = √3/4.

Required value = [(4 − √3)/2] ÷ [√3/4] = [(4 − √3)/2] × [4/√3] = 2(4 − √3) / √3 = (8 − 2√3) / √3.

**∴ The correct answer is (8 − 2√3) / √3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A = 30°

**Formula Used:** cos 2A = 2cos² A − 1 = 1 − 2sin² A

⇒ Simplify Numerator (N): cos 2A + 2cos² A − 2cos 2A cos A

⇒ N = cos 2A + (1 + cos 2A) − 2cos 2A cos A

⇒ N = 1 + 2cos 2A − 2cos 2A cos A = 1 + 2cos 2A (1 − cos A)

⇒ For A = 30°, N = 1 + 2cos 60° (1 − cos 30°) = 1 + 2(1/2) (1 − √3/2) = 1 + 1 − √3/2 = 2 − √3/2 = (4 − √3)/2

⇒ Simplify Denominator (D): sin 2A − 2sin² A sin 2A

⇒ D = sin 2A (1 − 2sin² A) = sin 2A cos 2A

⇒ For A = 30°, D = sin 60° cos 60° = (√3/2) × (1/2) = √3/4

⇒ Total Expression = N / D = [(4 − √3)/2] / [√3/4] = [(4 − √3)/2] × [4/√3]

⇒ Value = 2(4 − √3) / √3 = (8 − 2√3) / √3

**∴ The correct answer is (8 − 2√3) / √3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Double Angle Identities

cos 2A = cos² A − sin² A = 2cos² A − 1 = 1 − 2sin² A. Also, sin 2A = 2sin A cos A.

Standard Values at 30° and 60°

sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, sin 60° = √3/2, cos 60° = 1/2.

Half Angle Substitutions

cos² A = (1 + cos 2A) / 2 and sin² A = (1 − cos 2A) / 2 are often used to reduce powers of trig functions.</p

questions.question: What is the value of cos15° - cos165°?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the trigonometric identity: cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ.

Therefore, cos 165° = cos(180° − 15°) = −cos 15°.

The expression becomes cos 15° − (−cos 15°) = 2 cos 15°.

Given cos 15° = (√3 + 1) / (2√2), the value is 2 × [(√3 + 1) / (2√2)].

**∴ The correct answer is (√3 + 1) / √2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** cos 15° − cos 165°

**Formula Used:** cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C + D) / 2) sin((D − C) / 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c367fa9c2d574a01f04e3a946e18566fee554c55d85d6da82fcb8f0ef2c00bf.png] 

⇒ cos 15° − cos 165° = 2 sin((15° + 165°) / 2) sin((165° − 15°) / 2)

⇒ = 2 sin(180° / 2) sin(150° / 2)

⇒ = 2 sin 90° sin 75°

⇒ Since sin 90° = 1 and sin 75° = cos 15°

⇒ = 2 × 1 × [(√3 + 1) / (2√2)]

⇒ = (√3 + 1) / √2

**∴ The correct answer is (√3 + 1) / √2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Supplementary Angle Identities

cos(180° − θ) = −cos θ and sin(180° − θ) = sin θ. This is because in the second quadrant, cosine is negative while sine is positive.

Sum-to-Product Formula

cos C − cos D = 2 sin((C + D) / 2) sin((D − C) / 2). This formula helps convert the difference of two cosine functions into a product of sine functions.

Standard Values for 15° and 75°

cos 15° = sin 75° = (√3 + 1) / (2√2) and sin 15° = cos 75° = (√3 − 1) / (2√2).</p
